difficultyRationale: Tests whether the candidate knows the JPA-specified default fetch types differ by association cardinality, rather than assuming one default applies everywhere.
prompt: An `Order` entity has `@ManyToOne private Customer customer;` and `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "order") private List<OrderLine> lines;`, neither annotation specifying a `fetch` attribute. A service loads a list of 50 `Order` rows and only reads `order.getCustomer().getName()` for each, never touching `lines`. What does the JPA specification say the default fetch behavior is here, and what does it imply for this query?
explanation: The JPA specification gives single-valued associations (`@ManyToOne`, `@OneToOne`) a default `FetchType.EAGER` and collection-valued associations (`@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany`) a default `FetchType.LAZY`. So each `Order` row eagerly loads its `customer` (one join or one extra select per row, depending on the provider), while `lines` stays an uninitialized proxy collection that is never touched in this code path and therefore never queried.

options.text: Both `@ManyToOne` and `@OneToMany` default to `FetchType.LAZY`, so neither `customer` nor `lines` is loaded until a getter on either is actually called by the service code.
options.explanation: Only collection-valued associations default to LAZY. `@ManyToOne` defaults to EAGER by specification, so `customer` is loaded eagerly here regardless of whether the code reads it.

options.text: `@ManyToOne` defaults to `FetchType.EAGER` and `@OneToMany` defaults to `FetchType.LAZY`; `customer` loads with (or alongside) each `Order` row, while `lines` stays an unfetched proxy until accessed.
options.explanation: Correct per the JPA specification's default fetch types for `@ManyToOne`/`@OneToOne` (EAGER) versus `@OneToMany`/`@ManyToMany` (LAZY). This asymmetry is exactly why eagerly-defaulted single-valued associations are a common, easy-to-miss source of extra queries.

options.text: Both `@ManyToOne` and `@OneToMany` default to `FetchType.EAGER`, so this code already eagerly loads all 50 customers and the full `lines` collection for every order in one combined join.
options.explanation: Collection-valued associations default to LAZY, not EAGER. `lines` is not loaded here; only `customer` is, because `@ManyToOne` alone defaults to EAGER.

options.text: The JPA specification leaves the default fetch type for every association unspecified and provider-defined, so Hibernate, EclipseLink, and OpenJPA are each free to pick a different default for the same unannotated `@ManyToOne` field.
options.explanation: The specification does mandate default fetch types per association type (EAGER for single-valued, LAZY for collection-valued); this is not left to provider discretion, and every compliant provider follows it.

references.title: Jakarta Persistence Specification 3.1 — Javadoc, ManyToOne annotation (default FetchType.EAGER)
